newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical prices off $200 mln vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical prices off $200 mln vs yr ago.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co said Thursday it experienced a $200 million price decline compared with the second quarter of 1996, which was offset by worldwide volume growth, reduced operating expenses and the favorable impact of currency on costs.

Dow said prices were down in all geographies and all core business segments compared with a year ago, with the exception of plastics. Since the first quarter of 1997, however, price declines in most businesses have either slowed or stabilized.

Earlier, Dow Chemical reported earnings for the second quarter of $2.48 a share, up from $2.20 a year ago. The second quarter 1997 results included a net gain of $0.23 a share related to several one-time events.

These events included a gain on the sale of Dow's majority stake in Destec Inc, and charges related to insurance restructuring, the shutdown of an ethylene cracker in Texas, and charges DowElanco made at the time of the purchase of Eli Lilly and Co's 40 percent stake in this joint venture.
Excluding these one-time items, Dow's second quarter earnings were $2.25 a share.

"Dow's second quarter earnings improvement reflects the effect of the company's strategically balanced product portfolio, the impact of above average volume growth, and continued expense control," J. Pedro Reinhard, chief financial officer, said in a statement. "The improvement was achieved despite unfavorable currency effects and mixed prices."
Sales for the quarter were $5.4 billion, up four percent from a year ago. Volume gains of eight percent were partially offset by a four percent decline in prices, mostly from currency.
